# BVH build-order parity vectors (#7674, EDGE-CLASH-1).
#
# rust/clash/src/bvh.rs is a port of packages/spatial/src/bvh.ts. Both sides
# read this file: rust/clash/src/bvh_tests.rs and
# packages/spatial/src/bvh.parity.test.ts. The `=>` lists were produced by the
# TypeScript BVH, which is the reference; a query returns ids in depth-first
# leaf order, so the list pins the tree shape, not only the hit set.
#
# The split order is: centre along the split axis ascending, a NaN centre
# after every number, then the item's position in the input (not its id).
# That is a total order, so the sort cannot panic on NaN and both sides
# build the same tree.
#
# Format, whitespace separated, `#` starts a comment line:
#   case <name>
#   item <id> <minX> <minY> <minZ> <maxX> <maxY> <maxZ>
#   query <minX> <minY> <minZ> <maxX> <maxY> <maxZ> => <id> ...
# Numbers may be NaN, Infinity, -Infinity or -0 (Rust's f64 parser and JS
# Number() both accept those spellings).

case child-tie-broken-by-index
# root splits on X; the left child splits on Y where both centres tie, so
# input position decides (ids run backwards here), not the parent's X order
item 40 0.9 -5 -0.1 1.1 5 0.1
item 30 -0.1 -5 -0.1 0.1 5 0.1
item 20 19.9 -0.1 -0.1 20.1 0.1 0.1
item 10 20.9 -0.1 -0.1 21.1 0.1 0.1
query -1000000000 -1000000000 -1000000000 1000000000 1000000000 1000000000 => 40 30 20 10
query -1 -1 -1 2 1 1 => 40 30

case signed-zero-centres-tie
# centres -0 and +0 compare equal (index decides); total_cmp would put -0 first
item 0 -1 -1 -1 1 1 1
item 1 -0 -0.5 -0.5 -0 0.5 0.5
item 2 4.5 -0.5 -0.5 5.5 0.5 0.5
item 3 5.5 -0.5 -0.5 6.5 0.5 0.5
item 4 -5.5 -0.5 -0.5 -4.5 0.5 0.5
query -1000000000 -1000000000 -1000000000 1000000000 1000000000 1000000000 => 4 0 1 2 3
